healthcareSystem: Universal (e-card system for residents). EU/EEA citizens covered by European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). Others pay out-of-pocket or via travel insurance.
qualityNotes: High-quality healthcare available throughout the country. Major cities (Vienna, Salzburg, Innsbruck) have excellent hospitals with English-speaking staff. Rural areas may have limited English. Healthcare is significantly cheaper than Switzerland but still expensive by regional standards.
pharmacyHours: Typically Mon-Fri 8am-6pm, Sat 8am-12pm. Some pharmacies in cities offer on-call/emergency service (Apotheken-Notdienst). Look for 'Apotheke' signs — green cross.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacists often speak English in tourist areas. Many common OTC medications are available. EU prescriptions (red/blue slip) are accepted. Bring a European Health Insurance Card if you're an EU citizen.
prescriptionRules: EU/EEA prescriptions are accepted in Austria (blue EU prescription form). Prescriptions from outside the EU may require a local doctor to re-issue them. Schengen countries follow standardized prescription formats.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is a controlled substance. Products with codeine require a prescription or an Austrian doctor's approval. Small personal-use quantities may be permitted with documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled opioid. Requires Austrian prescription for extended use. Carry your original foreign prescription and doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines (e.g., Valium/diazepam, Xanax/alprazolam)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. EU regulations allow travelers to carry personal medications with a doctor's certificate. Austrian customs may inspect quantities.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is strictly controlled. Only available via Austrian prescription for specific conditions. CBD products with minimal THC are tolerated but not fully legal.

restrictedMeds.name: Methylphenidate (Ritalin)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled ADHD medication. Requires documentation if bringing for personal use. Austrian doctor consultation recommended upon arrival.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter (English or German) listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. EU citizens should carry the EHIC. Non-EU travelers should carry original prescriptions and a travel certificate.

travelInsurance.tips: EHIC covers EU citizens for emergency healthcare at public facilities. Non-EU travelers need comprehensive travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage. Emergency services are free at point of care for EHIC holders. Hospital stays can still be costly — insurance is essential.

vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations. Ensure routine immunizations are current. FSME (tick-borne encephalitis) vaccination is recommended if spending time outdoors in summer, especially in forested areas of Lower Austria, Styria, and Carinthia.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe and of excellent quality throughout Austria. Austrian mountain spring water is famously clean.
foodSafetyTips: Austria has high food safety standards. Traditional foods like Wiener Schnitzel, Tafelspitz, and Sachertorte are safe. Be cautious of wild mushrooms if foraging — poisoning from misidentified fungi is a real risk.
medicalTourismNote: Austria is known for spa towns (Bad Gastein, Bad Ischl) and wellness tourism. Dental tourism is also popular due to lower costs than Western Europe. Quality is high in major cities.
sources: Austrian Federal Ministry of Social Affairs, Health, Care and Consumer Protection
metaDescription: Health & medication guide for Austria. Emergency numbers (144/133/122), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, travel insurance advice, and vaccination recommendations.

hospitals.name: Allgemeines Krankenhaus Wien (AKH)
hospitals.notes: Vienna's main university hospital. One of Europe's largest. Full emergency department.

hospitals.name: Privatklinik Döbling
hospitals.notes: Private hospital with shorter wait times. English-speaking staff.

hospitals.name: Landeskrankenhaus Salzburg
hospitals.notes: Regional hospital near Salzburg's tourist center.

hospitals.name: Universitätsklinik Innsbruck
hospitals.notes: Excellent for mountain/ski injuries. University hospital with trauma center.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Excellent dental care available throughout Austria. EU citizens can access emergency dental care with EHIC.
dentalCare.costRange: €50-100 for a consultation; €80-250 for fillings; €100-300 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Austrian dental care is high quality. Many dentists in Vienna and tourist areas speak English. Dental tourism is growing due to lower costs than Germany or Switzerland.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies outside business hours, call the Zahnärztlicher Notdienst (dental emergency service) at 01-512-20-78 in Vienna. Hospital emergency departments can provide pain relief.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: Crisis Text Line: text HOME to 741741 (English)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: English-speaking therapists available in Vienna through international practices. Check Psychology Today's international directory.
mentalHealth.notes: Austria has good mental healthcare but services in English are mainly available in Vienna. Most therapists work by appointment. ÖGK (public insurance) covers some therapy sessions for residents.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Austria has solid accessibility infrastructure. Major cities comply with EU accessibility standards. Historic buildings may have limited access.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Modern hospitals are fully wheelchair accessible. Older clinics in historic buildings may have limited access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Vienna's U-Bahn is fully wheelchair accessible. ÖBB trains offer accessible carriages. Taxis with wheelchair access available by request.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Book accessible accommodations in advance, especially in alpine areas. Ski resorts often have adaptive skiing programs. Vienna's tourist office provides accessibility guides.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates in public spaces. Masks may be required in healthcare facilities during respiratory illness season.
covidStatus.testing: PCR and antigen tests available at pharmacies and clinics. Cost: €25-80 for PCR.
covidStatus.notes: Austria lifted all COVID restrictions. Healthcare facilities may have seasonal mask requirements.

insuranceClaimProcess: EU citizens with EHIC receive emergency care at public hospitals at no upfront cost. Non-EU travelers: keep all Rechnung (invoices) and Befund (medical reports). Request English documentation. Private clinics may require payment upfront — get an itemized invoice for insurance claims.
